Name: Effortless CLI
Description: Rulebook for the effortless CLI (binary aliases: effortless, ssotme, aicapture, aic): every command-line option, the request-handling state machine, the REST wire contract with transpiler tools, every config file and endpoint, the module map, the user messages tests assert on, and the full test plan. This file is the single source of truth: CliOptions, bareword verbs, option metadata, the CLI reference, the README command block and the test manifests are generated from it.

Dispositions.Description: Whether a behaviour is carried unchanged (keep) or with a deliberate, documented difference from the previous release (keep-modified). Every other table with a Disposition column points here.

schema.Description: Slug identifying the disposition.

schema.name: Label
schema.Description: Human-readable label.

schema.name: IsRetained
schema.Description: True when the artifact carries forward into the new build (possibly modified).

schema.name: NeedsUserConfirmation
schema.Description: True when this is a recommendation, not a settled decision; the owner must confirm before the corresponding refactor step runs.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What this disposition means and how Opus should treat rows that carry it.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias for the row; mirrors DispositionId.

schema.name: CountOfCliOptions
schema.Description: How many CLI options carry this disposition.

schema.name: CountOfSourceModules
schema.Description: How many rows across the tables carry this disposition.

schema.name: CountOfHttpEndpoints
schema.Description: How many remote endpoints carry this disposition.

A build that names a local tool starts an ephemeral host for the duration of the build; serve keeps one running so repeated builds reuse it.

CliOptions.Description: This table is the source of truth for the generated options class, the generated CLI reference, the -help output, and test coverage (CountOfTestCases).

schema.name: CliOptionId
schema.Description: The C# property name of the option (also the primary flag without the dash).

schema.name: Flag
schema.Description: Primary flag as typed by the user.

schema.name: Aliases
schema.Description: Comma-separated Plossum aliases (verbatim from the designer file; empty when none).

schema.name: BarewordForms
schema.Description: Comma-separated bare verbs accepted as the FIRST positional argument (from FixParameters; matched case-insensitively after ToLower). Empty when none.

schema.name: ValueType
schema.Description: bool, string, int or list (List<string>).

schema.name: HelpText
schema.Description: Verbatim Description shown by -help. MUST be preserved character-for-character for retained options.

schema.name: Category
schema.Description: Functional grouping.

schema.name: Disposition
schema.Description: keep (unchanged behaviour) or keep-modified (a deliberate, documented difference from the previous release).

schema.name: IsCommand
schema.Description: True when the option selects an action (a verb); false when it modifies another action.

schema.name: ConsumesNextArgAsTool
schema.Description: True when the bareword form takes the next positional argument as the tool/value (FixParameters sets transpiler = args[1] for every matched verb; for setUrl/viewUrl/removeUrl the value is also copied into the option).

schema.name: HandlerNotes
schema.Description: How the option is implemented in the code, in one or two sentences.

schema.name: DispositionReason
schema.Description: Why it gets this disposition; for keep-modified, the exact change.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: Plain-English meaning for docs.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias for the row; mirrors Flag.

schema.name: IsRetained
schema.Description: Whether the option survives into the new build.

schema.name: NeedsUserConfirmation
schema.Description: Whether the owner must confirm this disposition.

schema.name: CategoryLabel
schema.Description: Heading for docs.

schema.name: CountOfTestCases
schema.Description: Number of planned test cases whose primary subject is this option.

schema.name: IsTested
schema.Description: True when at least one test case targets this option.

schema.name: IsRetainedButUntested
schema.Description: Coverage gap flag: retained options with no test are not allowed to reach

schema.name: Tier
schema.Description: primary (day-one verb), secondary (real but occasional), modifier (only meaningful with a parent command), or plumbing (for scripts/CI/tooling).

schema.name: ParentOption
schema.Description: For a modifier: the CliOptionId of the command it modifies.

schema.name: VerbFamily
schema.Description: build, clean, or describe for verb-family members sharing the downstream/Local/All/WithSubprojects pattern; null otherwise.

schema.name: Scope
schema.Description: downstream, local, all, or withSubprojects: which of the four verb-family scopes this row is, when VerbFamily is set.

schema.name: Rationale
schema.Description: The owner's why-this-exists for the option, drawn from DispositionReason/HandlerNotes and the step-09 decision table.

schema.name: HelpSummary
schema.Description: One line, at most 72 characters, shown in the default -help listing.

schema.name: HelpDetail
schema.Description: Shown by -help <option> and in the generated cli-reference.md; the full explanation, aliases, and quirks.

schema.name: Example
schema.Description: One realistic invocation of the option.

data.HelpText: Show help about how to use the Effortless CLI
data.HandlerNotes: ParseCommand: prints parser.UsageInfo header + "Syntax: effortless [account/]transpiler [Options]" + options; SuppressTranspile.
data.DispositionReason: -help becomes grouped by category/tier and filterable (-help <category|option>, -help all) instead of one flat list of every option; behavior implemented in a later phase.
data.Description: Print usage.
data.Rationale: Every CLI needs a self-describing entry point; this is where the option taxonomy (tiers, categories, families) actually gets surfaced to a user.
data.HelpSummary: Show usage and available commands
data.HelpDetail: Prints primary-tier commands grouped by category. `-help <category|option>` narrows to one topic; `-help all` prints the flat list of every option regardless of tier.

data.HelpText: Initialize the current folder as the root of an Effortless project. An Optional parameter of force will create a sub-project.
data.HandlerNotes: ParseCommand: projectName defaults to cwd name; force = (args.Length==2 && args[1]=="force"); AICaptureProject.Init(force, name); also registers a ProjectTranspiler for compile-rulebook (RelativePath=/effortless-rulebook, CommandLine="compile-rulebook -i effortless-rulebook.json"); then continueToLoad=true and build=true (init implies a build).
data.DispositionReason: Modified only in that "force" must work through the npm shim too (argv passthrough); output identical.
data.Description: Create effortless.json, .gitignore, effortless.env, a starter rulebook, and register compile-rulebook against it, in cwd.
data.Rationale: The first command any new project runs; creates the effortless.json/rulebook scaffold a build needs to exist at all.
data.HelpSummary: Create effortless.json and a starter rulebook here
data.HelpDetail: Initializes the current folder as an Effortless project root. Writes effortless.json and a starter effortless-rulebook/effortless-rulebook.json containing one HelloWho entity with a raw Who field, a calculated Result field ("Hello " & Who & "!"), and three rows, and registers the compile-rulebook transpiler against it, so the project builds and produces real output before you have written any rules of your own. Pass `force` as the next argument to create a nested sub-project instead of failing when a parent project already exists.

data.HelpText: Saves the current command into the Effortless Project file
data.HandlerNotes: Runs the tool first (StartTranspile/SaveFileSet) then Install() in the finally block; URL tools install without running; ShouldAutoBuildForInstall builds first when -i file is missing; ProjectTranspiler ctor captures Environment.CommandLine and strips exe/verb prefixes.
data.Description: Register a transpiler step in effortless.json (and run it once).
data.Rationale: How a transpiler step becomes part of the project rather than a one-off run; every build depends on steps registered this way.
data.HelpSummary: Register a transpiler step in effortless.json
data.HelpDetail: Runs the named tool once and, on success, saves it as a step in effortless.json so future builds include it. Combine with -transpilerGroup to tag the step into a group.

data.HelpText: Removes the current command from the Effortless Project file
data.HandlerNotes: Name from RemainingArguments[0]; EffortlessProject.Uninstall matches by short/qualified name + cwd RelativePath + optional -tg; prompts y/n to clean when a .zfs exists.
data.Description: Remove a registered step.
data.Rationale: The inverse of install; needed whenever a project's pipeline changes.
data.HelpSummary: Remove a registered step from effortless.json
data.HelpDetail: Removes the named step from the current folder's effortless.json entries, matching by tool name and (optionally) -transpilerGroup. Offers to clean the step's previous output first.

data.HelpText: Build any transpilers in the current folder (or children).
data.HandlerNotes: TranspileProject: BuildErrorLog.Begin("build"); project.Rebuild(cwd, includeDisabled, tg, buildOnTrigger, copilotConnect, buildLocal=false, debug, continueOnError); Finish.
data.Description: Run every enabled step at or below cwd.
data.Rationale: The core day-one verb: runs every enabled step at or below the current folder. The build/clean pair and their All/Local/WithSubprojects scopes are the whole project-pipeline family (D12).
data.HelpSummary: Build steps in this folder and its children
data.HelpDetail: Runs every enabled transpiler step registered at or below the current folder (downstream scope). Use -buildLocal for exactly this folder, -buildAll for the whole project, or -buildWithSubprojects to also include nested effortless projects.

data.HelpText: Builds all transpilers in the project
data.HandlerNotes: RebuildAll from RootPath (isBuildAll=true). D6/D12: nested effortless.json subprojects are NOT traversed; that moved to buildWithSubprojects, which passes withSubprojects=true and drives NestedProjectFinder + ChildProcessRunner.
data.DispositionReason: behavior change: All now means strictly "as if run from the project root". Sub-project builds still spawn the current executable by path instead of "effortless" from PATH.
data.Description: Run every step in the whole project, excluding nested effortless projects.
data.Rationale: D6/D12: runs the project as if invoked from its root, without walking into nested effortless.json subprojects (which are normally excluded and require -buildWithSubprojects).
data.HelpSummary: Build the whole project from its root
data.HelpDetail: Builds every step in the project as if run from the project root, regardless of the current folder. Nested effortless.json subprojects are excluded (spawned separately via -buildLocal in each); use -buildWithSubprojects to include them.

data.HelpText: Build only the transpilers installed in the current folder
data.HandlerNotes: IsAtPath(exactMatch:true); also skips the parent-root-seed check.
data.Description: Run only steps whose RelativePath equals cwd.
data.Rationale: The exact-folder scope of the build family (D12); used when you only want to run what is registered right here, ignoring child folders.
data.HelpSummary: Build only steps registered exactly here
data.HelpDetail: Runs only the steps whose RelativePath equals the current folder exactly, ignoring child folders and skipping the parent-root-seed check.

data.HelpText: Builds whenever a trigger is invoked (see readme for URL)
data.HandlerNotes: TriggerBuildWatcher polls the live Airtable bridge every 3s and rebuilds after 10 quiet seconds. HTTP, status, or JSON failures stop the watcher with non-zero status; there is no silent polling fallback.
data.DispositionReason: Owner decision keep the lightweight cloud-trigger monitor independently of effortless-rulebook-editor.
data.Rationale: D24: a lightweight, dependency-free way to watch a cloud source (Airtable today) for changes without running a whole editor/Docker stack. Kept as its own small polling loop precisely because that is not overkill for common single-purpose use cases.
data.HelpSummary: Rebuild automatically when a remote trigger fires
data.HelpDetail: Polls the Airtable change-trigger bridge for the given base id every few seconds and rebuilds after a quiet period once it reports a change. Independent of the effortless-rulebook-editor's own change detection. Polling, HTTP, or payload failures are fatal, not a silently-ignored 'unchanged' result.

data.HelpText: Show debug output
data.HandlerNotes: Gates DEBUG: lines everywhere; appended as " -debug" to every build step command line; makes SavePreviousFileSet also write <tool>.xml; shows debug-level tool logs.
data.Description: Verbose diagnostics.
data.Rationale: Verbose diagnostics for scripts, CI, and troubleshooting a failed build; not something a first-time user reaches for.
data.HelpSummary: Print verbose diagnostics for this invocation
data.HelpDetail: Turns on DEBUG output across the build, appends -debug to every spawned step's command line, and writes an extra debug XML fileset snapshot alongside normal output.

data.HelpText: Describe the transpilers in the current folder and its children
data.HandlerNotes: v2 behavior change: project.Describe(cwd) now filters by IsAtOrBelowPath(cwd) instead of IsAtPath(exactMatch:true), matching the build/clean downstream convention. The old local-only behavior moves to the new describeLocal row. QUIRK preserved: bareword "list" means describe, while flag -list means listVersions.
data.DispositionReason: describe joins the build/clean verb-family pattern.
data.Rationale: D12/D23: describe is the steps view of a project; joining the build/clean verb family (D12) means it now defaults to downstream scope instead of local-only, matching how build already behaves.
data.HelpSummary: Describe steps in this folder and its children

data.HelpText: Describe all of the transpiler in the project
data.HandlerNotes: project.Describe() unfiltered.
data.Description: Print the whole project.
data.Rationale: D23: describe is the steps view of a project; describeAll is its whole-project scope, unfiltered by folder.
data.HelpSummary: Print the whole project's steps, unfiltered
data.HelpDetail: Prints every step in the project regardless of folder.

data.HelpText: Input filename or comma separated list of file names
data.HandlerNotes: LoadInputFiles/ImportFile: comma split, "newname=pattern" rename, trailing "?" marks optional, directory part validated against project scope (parent project allowed), glob via DirectoryInfo.GetFiles(pattern); binary detected by control chars; contents zipped.
data.Description: Input file(s) sent to the tool.
data.Rationale: The explicit way to send specific files to a tool instead of relying on its own fileset discovery; used by scripted/CI invocations and by -execute-adjacent local tooling.
data.HelpSummary: Send specific input file(s) to the tool
data.HelpDetail: Comma-separated file names or glob patterns sent to the tool. Supports `newname=pattern` renaming and a trailing `?` to mark a file optional.

data.HelpText: Output filename
data.HandlerNotes: Copied into payload.CLIOutput.
data.Description: Requested output filename for the tool.
data.Rationale: D21: output shape is the tool's call, not the CLI's — a tool may write one file or a whole tree. The CLI's only job is to pass the requested name through.
data.HelpSummary: Requested output name, passed through to the tool
data.HelpDetail: Whatever the tool decides: the CLI passes this value to the tool as OutputFileName and does not interpret, validate, or default it. The tool may use it as a single file name or as the root of a directory tree it writes.

data.HelpText: Clean all transpilers installed in and downstream of this folder
data.HandlerNotes: Three branches: with a .zfs given via -i (clean that ledger); with no remaining args (project.Clean(cwd, preserveZFS, purge, debug) + reverse seed replacements); with a tool name (result.CleanFileSet instead of SaveFileSet after running).
data.Description: Delete generated files recorded in .zfs ledgers.
data.Rationale: The build/clean pair is the core loop; clean removes what a previous build wrote so the next build starts from a known state.
data.HelpSummary: Delete generated output here and below
data.HelpDetail: Deletes files recorded in the .zfs ledger for every step registered at or below the current folder. Combine with -purge to also clean orphaned ledgers for steps no longer registered, or -preserveZFS to keep the ledger files themselves.

data.HelpText: Clean all project transpilers
data.HandlerNotes: CleanRunner.CleanAll from RootPath (cleanAll=true). D6/D12: nested effortless.json subprojects are NOT traversed; that moved to cleanWithSubprojects, which passes withSubprojects=true.
data.DispositionReason: behavior change: All now means strictly "as if run from the project root".
data.Description: Clean the whole project, excluding nested effortless projects.
data.Rationale: D12: the whole-project scope of clean, mirroring buildAll; also removes empty folders left behind.
data.HelpSummary: Clean the whole project from its root
data.HelpDetail: Cleans every step's output across the whole project (spawning -clean in nested effortless.json subprojects) and removes folders left empty afterward.

data.HelpText: Cleans only transpilers installed in the current folder
data.HandlerNotes: IsAtPath(exactMatch:true).
data.Description: Clean only steps registered exactly at cwd.
data.Rationale: D12: the exact-folder scope of clean, mirroring buildLocal.
data.HelpSummary: Clean only steps registered exactly here
data.HelpDetail: Cleans only the steps whose RelativePath equals the current folder exactly.

data.HelpText: When supplied with clean, runs clean on all orphaned transpilers
data.HandlerNotes: RemoveUnusedZFSFiles: any .zfs under .effortless not matching a current step is cleaned (in its RelativePath) then deleted, plus its debug .xml. Only when !preserveZFS.
data.Description: Also clean ledgers of steps that are no longer registered.
data.Rationale: Keeps a project's .effortless ledger directory from accumulating stale entries for steps that were uninstalled without ever being cleaned.
data.HelpSummary: Also delete ledgers for steps no longer registered
data.HelpDetail: When passed with clean, any .zfs ledger under .effortless that no longer corresponds to a currently-registered step is cleaned (its recorded output files are deleted) and then the ledger file itself is removed, along with its debug XML. Has no effect when -preserveZFS is also set.

data.HelpText: Don't clean the output before cooking
data.HandlerNotes: SaveFileSet(skipClean): skips CleanFileSet of the previous .zfs before writing.
data.Description: Write outputs without first cleaning the previous run.
data.Rationale: Lets a tool run write outputs on top of whatever is already there instead of first deleting the previous run's files; useful when a tool's own output is additive or when a previous clean already ran.
data.HelpSummary: Write outputs without cleaning the previous ones
data.HelpDetail: Skips deleting the files recorded in the previous .zfs ledger before a step writes its new output. The previous output is left in place; anything the new run does not overwrite survives untouched.

data.HelpText: Lists public Effortless seed repositories across the seed sources
data.HandlerNotes: SeedCommands.List: with no argument lists every seed source in order, grouped by account with descriptions; with an account argument lists that account only. A seed is a public repository with effortless.json at its root (SeedCatalogClient checks the raw default-branch file). GitHub API failures are fatal.
data.DispositionReason: Owner decision root and child Effortless repositories remain first-class seeds.
data.Description: List public Effortless seed repositories across the configured seed sources.
data.Rationale: D25: seed discovery is real but occasional — used when scaffolding a new project from an existing public Effortless repository, not on every-day builds.
data.HelpSummary: List seeds across every seed source
data.HelpDetail: Lists every public repository with effortless.json at its root under each configured seed source (see listSeedSources), grouped by account with the repository description. Pass an account name to list only that account.

data.HelpText: Clones a public Effortless seed repository (account/repo, repo, or clone URL)
data.HandlerNotes: SeedCommands.Clone: <account>/<repo> clones that repository; a bare <repo> searches the seed sources in order and clones the single match, printing the account it came from; the same name matching in more than one source (or matching both a full and short name in one) is an ambiguity error listing every candidate; an http(s) URL is cloned directly. Argument-safe git clone preserving .git; verifies effortless.json at the root; never runs cloned code; prints the explicit build command. Optional second argument is the destination directory.
data.DispositionReason: Owner decision . Modernized to preserve .git and avoid executing downloaded code without a separate user action.
data.Description: Clone a public Effortless seed repository.
data.Rationale: D25: the other half of seed discovery — turning a listed seed into a local starting project.
data.HelpSummary: Clone a public Effortless seed repository
data.HelpDetail: Clones the seed and verifies effortless.json at its root. Accepts account/repo, a bare repository name (searched across the seed sources in order; an ambiguous name lists the candidates), or an HTTP(S) clone URL; an optional second argument names the destination directory. Preserves .git and never executes cloned code; prints the build command to run next.

data.HelpText: The account which the transpiler belongs to
data.HandlerNotes: Also auto-extracted from "acct/tool" names when no URL resolves. D20: resolution never fails on acct/tool alone - if acct/tool does not resolve in the catalog, the CLI resolves tool and behaves as tool -account acct, failing only if tool itself does not resolve either. Drives credential injection: effortless.env {ACCOUNT}_{PAT|API_KEY|APIKEY|KEY}->apiKey, {ACCOUNT}_{BASEID|BASE_ID}->baseId, else effortless.key APIKeys[account]->apiKey (JSON-valued key => error). Sent as cliAccount.
data.DispositionReason: acct/tool extraction behavior is changing from an implicit fallback to a documented never-fail contract (ToolResolutionRules R6/R7).
data.Description: Credential/account selector for a tool.
data.Rationale: D19/D20: selects which stored credentials apply to a tool invocation, whether given explicitly or extracted from an `acct/tool` name.
data.HelpSummary: Account whose stored credentials apply to this tool
data.HelpDetail: Selects the account used for credential injection (see -setAccountAPIKey) and is also auto-extracted from an `acct/tool` name when the combined name does not resolve in the catalog (D20: resolution then falls back to `tool -account acct` instead of failing).

data.HelpText: A list of parameters
data.HandlerNotes: Sent as cliParams; extra positional args become param{n}=value; ProjectSettings appended as name=value unless already present; account credentials appended last (replacing same-named entries).
data.Description: key=value parameters for the tool.
data.Rationale: The general-purpose way to pass key=value data into a tool invocation without a dedicated flag for every possible input.
data.HelpSummary: key=value parameters passed to the tool
data.HelpDetail: A comma-separated list of key=value pairs sent to the tool as cliParams. Extra positional arguments become param0, param1, etc. Project settings and account credentials are appended automatically, with credentials taking precedence on a name collision.

data.HelpText: List of project settings
data.HandlerNotes: project.ListSettings(): "SETTINGS:" then "    - name = value" or "NO settings added to the project yet."
data.Description: Print ProjectSettings.
data.Rationale: D23: project settings (persistent key=value values on the project) are a distinct concept from user-level state (info) and from steps (describe); this prints just that layer.
data.HelpSummary: List this project's settings
data.HelpDetail: Prints every ProjectSetting stored in effortless.json, or a message that none have been added yet.

data.HelpText: Adds a setting to the Effortless Project
data.HandlerNotes: project.AddSetting("name=value") per item then Save; "project-name" also renames the project; missing name => exception.
data.Description: Add/replace a ProjectSetting.
data.Rationale: The write side of project settings; used to configure a project once rather than repeat a parameter on every build.
data.HelpSummary: Add or replace a project setting
data.HelpDetail: Adds a name=value ProjectSetting to effortless.json, replacing any existing setting with the same name. The special name `project-name` renames the project instead.

data.HelpText: Removes a setting from the Effortless Project
data.HandlerNotes: project.RemoveSetting(name) then Save; unknown => exception "Can't find matching setting".
data.Description: Remove a ProjectSetting.
data.Rationale: The inverse of addSetting; needed whenever a project setting is no longer wanted.
data.HelpSummary: Remove a project setting
data.HelpDetail: Removes the named ProjectSetting from effortless.json. Fails clearly when no setting with that name exists.

data.HelpText: The amount of time to wait for the command to continue
data.HandlerNotes: Default 180000 ms; HttpClient.Timeout, retry loop budget, waitForCook bound, -execute WaitForExit; sent as cliWaitTimeout.
data.Description: Timeout in milliseconds.
data.Rationale: Controls how long the CLI will wait on a slow or cold-starting remote tool before giving up; mainly a knob for scripts and CI against slow workloads.
data.HelpSummary: Timeout in milliseconds for the tool call
data.HelpDetail: Bounds the HTTP client timeout, the retry-loop budget, and (for -execute) how long a local process is given to exit. Defaults to 180000 ms (3 minutes). Sent to the tool as cliWaitTimeout.

data.HelpText: Run as this user (look for this user's key file)
data.HandlerNotes: Selects ~/.effortless/effortless.{runAs}.key for GetKey/SetKey (info, setAccountAPIKey, account lookup, StartTranspile).
data.DispositionReason: Cheap and coherent with -setAccountAPIKey multi-account key files.
data.Description: Use an alternate key file.
data.Rationale: D7: cheap to keep and coherent with -setAccountAPIKey's multi-account key files; useful for CI or shared machines running as more than one identity.
data.HelpSummary: Use an alternate user's key file
data.HelpDetail: Selects ~/.effortless/effortless.<user>.key instead of the default key file for this invocation, matching whatever account key was stored under that user with -setAccountAPIKey -runAs <user>.

data.HelpText: Determines if the input should be preserved.
data.HandlerNotes: Clean keeps the .zfs ledger files; also disables -purge.
data.Description: Keep .zfs ledgers when cleaning.
data.Rationale: Lets a clean remove generated files while keeping the ledger record of what was written, useful when you want to re-run clean logic without losing the manifest, or you distrust deleting the ledger itself.
data.HelpSummary: Keep the .zfs ledger files when cleaning
data.HelpDetail: Clean still deletes the generated output files it finds recorded, but keeps the .zfs ledger file itself instead of deleting it. Also disables -purge, since purge's whole point is removing orphaned ledgers.

data.HelpText: Executes the given command as a ProcessInfo.Start
data.HandlerNotes: ProcessCommandLine: first token is the executable, rest are args; WaitForExit(waitTimeout); Win32Exception => NoStackException "The system couldn't find the command"; with -install registers a "LocalCommand" step whose CommandLine starts with -execute.
data.DispositionReason: Local build steps are REST-agnostic and used by projects.
data.Description: Run a local command as a (registered) step.
data.Rationale: D26: a shell step with no fileset is a real, distinct need from a REST tool call — local build tooling (compilers, scripts, package managers) that isn't fileset-aware. Step 12's local transpiler host coexists with this rather than replacing it.
data.HelpSummary: Run a local command as a (registered) step
data.HelpDetail: Runs the given command line as a child process, waiting up to -waitTimeout for it to exit. Combine with -install to register it as a LocalCommand step that runs on every future build.

data.HelpText: Include disabled tools in the build

When they differ, always asks Yes/No/Always/Never: Yes reinstalls once via npm install -g @effortlessapi/cli@latest; No skips this time; Always reinstalls now and remembers to auto-reinstall silently in the once-daily background check (see update-check-background); Never remembers to skip the background check until you run -checkVersion again.

data.HelpText: Pin this project's step to a specific catalog version or URL
data.HandlerNotes: New in v2 (D17). Stores a hard pin (a catalog version key or a literal URL) on this project's installed step in effortless.json (PinnedVersion), distinct from the per-user -setToolUrl override which applies machine-wide across every project. IMPORTANT: ProjectToolFreshness.Apply takes clearPins; the automatic build-time gate (CommandDispatcher.EnsureProjectToolsCurrent) passes false so a deliberate pin survives a build, while -upgrade/-upgradeAll pass true and unpin. Without that split the gate would null PinnedVersion on every build and -pin could never take effect. Invocation shapes: the flag form is 'effortless <tool> -pin <version|url>'; the bareword form 'effortless pin <tool> <version|url>' is normalized by CliArgumentParser.NoDashCommandForms into the flag form (the trailing value becomes -pin's value and the tool stays in the tool position). 'pin <tool>' with no value falls through to Plossum, which reports "Missing required value for option pin".
data.DispositionReason: a step is either pinned or it follows HEAD. -pin is the explicit way to fix a version or URL for this project; -upgrade (alias unpin) or -upgradeAll clear it. Default stays unpinned = HEAD; pin-on-install by default is not assumed.
data.Description: Pin an installed step to a version or URL for this project.
data.Rationale: D17: gives a project a way to freeze a step's version deliberately (reproducibility, a known-good release) without reaching for the per-user -setToolUrl override, which is not project-scoped.
data.HelpSummary: Pin an installed step to a version or URL
data.HelpDetail: Pins the named step (already registered in this project) to either a specific catalog version key or a literal URL. Future builds of this project use the pin instead of HEAD until -upgrade (alias unpin) removes it.

data.HelpSummary: Host this project's local tools over HTTP

Records the port and pid in .effortless/serve.json so builds in this project reuse the running host instead of starting an ephemeral one. Reloads when effortless-tools/ changes. GET / lists the tools.

data.Result: Force ONE catalog refresh ignoring the 24h stamp (same bridge call as R0; failure is fatal, no stale fallback). Bound: at most one forced refresh per CLI invocation for one-shot commands no matter how many steps time out; long-running modes (buildOnTrigger, serve) at most once per 10 minutes. Excluded: -targetUrl, bare URLs, tool_urls.json overrides, local tools (they never consult the catalog, IsCatalogResolved=false).

_meta._CMCC_Summary: Hand-authored (LLM-direct) rulebook describing a software system — the effortless CLI — rather than a business domain. Tables are the nouns of the CLI (options, states, files, endpoints, tests, steps); calculated/lookup/aggregation fields expose coverage and retention facts (IsRetained, IsTested, IsRetainedButUntested, CountOfTestCases) so gaps are queryable.

_conversion_metadata.source: Hand-authored for the Effortless CLI v2 (REST-only) and maintained alongside the code; CliOptions, BarewordVerbs, the CLI reference, README command block and test manifests are generated from it by scripts/generate-from-rulebook.mjs.
